interpretation: Reading B (universal), second half: 'whenever it is true or false' read not as a condition but as saying that thought, in affirming or denying any object, is thereby true or false. Together with the first half this is bivalence for thought: every proposition is the object of some true or false thought. The verified result ARIST-MET-1012A-THOUGHT-BIVALENCE-IFF-EXCLUDED-MIDDLE shows that, given readings A and the composition premise, this is equivalent to excluded middle, so on this reading the passage restates the law rather than arguing for it against someone who withholds it.
